clue.text: Old ruler placed next to centre of graph

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, here the inner three of graph

explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in ancient Persia, so an old ruler of a province.

clue.text: Strength of Reds perhaps having switched ends

indicators.note: switched ends means the first and last letters change places

parts.note: reds are an example of wines, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: The power of a football team called the Reds after they changed ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having switched ends' swaps the W and S of WINES. 'Reds' suggests a sports team; here it is wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew is tendon, and figuratively muscular power or strength.

clue.text: Prompt maths registration set up

parts.note: trig is short for trigonometry, a branch of maths

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word is turned to read upwards

parts.note: reg is short for registration, as on a vehicle number plate

explanation.surface: A reminder to sign up for a maths course.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to set it off, cause or prompt it.

clue.text: Lonely single approaches 'Dateline' in excitement

indicators.note: approaches means coming up to, so it sits ahead of the next part

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dateline' was a well-known dating agency, fitting the lonely single.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling alienated means isolated and estranged from others, thus lonely.

clue.text: Blood disorder finally beat husband … he's out of shape

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word beat
he refers back to the husband, so his letter is taken out of the shape that follows

parts.note: a rhombus is a shape, an equal-sided parallelogram

explanation.walkthrough: 'he's out of' removes H from RHOMBUS, leaving ROMBUS; the 'he' is the husband already mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrombus is a clot formed in a blood vessel, a disorder of the blood's flow.

clue.text: Plant area stood on by crowd

explanation.definitionFit: A hosta is a leafy garden perennial, a type of plant.

clue.text: Large empty sphere over Easter regularly eaten

indicators.note: empty means the inside is removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very overweight, so a euphemistic sense of large.

clue.text: Fruit from edges of espalier stuffed into cheeses

indicators.note: edges of means the first and last letters of espalier

explanation.walkthrough: An espalier is a fruit tree trained flat against a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Berries are small fleshy fruits, so an example of fruit.

clue.text: Extremely specific search for bunch of players

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, first and last, of specific

explanation.surface: A very precise hunt for a group of performers.
explanation.walkthrough: A scrummage is the rugby scrum, where forwards bind together.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrummage is a rugby set piece in which forwards pack together, a bunch of players.

clue.text: Suffering briefly after held in US facility

indicators.note: after means this part follows the next one in the answer

explanation.walkthrough: PENT comes first, then AGON, AGONY shortened by 'briefly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pentagon is the US Department of Defense headquarters building, an American facility.

clue.text: Curiosity about icosahedron's original volume

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word is wrapped round the letter

parts.note: curiosity about others' business is nosiness

indicators.note: original means the first letter of icosahedron

explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' looks like a geometry word to go with icosahedron, but it means loudness here.
explanation.definitionFit: Volume in the sense of loudness is the amount of din, so it equals a racket's level.

clue.text: Brat hasn't time to make mistake

indicators.note: hasn't means the letter for time is missing from the word

parts.note: a little terror is a brat

explanation.surface: A spoilt child doesn't have time to slip up.
explanation.definitionFit: Error is a direct synonym for a mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Metal within secured carriage

indicators.note: within puts the metal inside the word for secured

parts.note: secured, as in gained a prize, gives WON
AG is the chemical symbol for silver, a metal

explanation.surface: Metal fittings inside a vehicle that has been fastened down.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a horse-drawn or railway carriage for goods or people.

clue.text: A prize mutt without tail circles quadrangle

without tail means the last letter of mutt is dropped

explanation.surface: A prize-winning dog with a docked tail runs round a courtyard.

clue.text: Plan of rogue on street to get a diamond?

parts.note: a rat is a rogue or scoundrel
a diamond is an example of a gem, hence the question mark

explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning scheme or plan to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Boring Maggie is half of an awkward couple

parts.note: square means old-fashioned and dull, boring
Peg is a pet form of Margaret, as is Maggie

explanation.surface: Dull Maggie is one partner of a mismatched pair.
explanation.walkthrough: The awkward couple is a square peg and a round hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A square peg in a round hole is a misfit; the peg is one member of that ill-matched pair.

clue.text: Commitment to one day on alternative male yoga

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the day sits on top of what follows

parts.note: MON is the abbreviation for Monday, a day

indicators.note: alternative suggests a different arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: One day a week devoted to a different kind of men's yoga.
explanation.definitionFit: Monogamy is having only one partner, a commitment to a single spouse.

clue.text: Where caffeine's served two functions mostly

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: cos and tan are two trigonometric functions, cosine and tangent

explanation.surface: A café that offers two uses, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: Costa Coffee is a big British coffee-shop chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Costa branch is a coffee shop, a place where caffeinated drinks are sold.

clue.text: Draw curves with these school idiots

parts.note: a comp is a comprehensive, a British state secondary school
asses are fools or idiots

explanation.definitionFit: Compasses are hinged drawing instruments for marking arcs and circles.

clue.text: Overturn suspension of writer by university director

indicators.note: suspension means the writer hangs between the two letters that follow

parts.note: a pen is something to write with

explanation.surface: A university head suspends an author from their post.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it upside down, to overturn it.

clue.text: Ban European medic boarding fabulous Greek ship

indicators.note: boarding means getting on to the ship, so the medic comes just ahead of the vessel

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, stands for a doctor
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek legend, so fabulous in the sense of mythical

clue.text: Ten Roman men naked running short distance

naked means stripped of the outer letters, leaving only the middle of men

explanation.surface: Ten unclothed Roman men streak a little way.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanometre is a billionth of a metre, an extremely small length.

clue.text: Haircut in Peru's notably retro

the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown of a monk or priest, a particular haircut.

clue.text: Heather on bishop during dance: it's revolting!

clue.text: Weapon material incorporates nucleus of uranium

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric, a material

indicators.note: nucleus means the central letter of uranium

explanation.surface: A weapons-grade material holding a uranium core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nucleus' and 'material' suggest nuclear physics; they are a middle letter and fabric.

clue.text: Central core of cylinder right under cone's lower section

core means the middle letters of cylinder

parts.note: taken as the word cone, whose top two letters are removed

explanation.definitionFit: Inner means situated inside or towards the centre, so central.

clue.text: Attach historic Queen number

parts.note: Queen Anne reigned over Britain in the early eighteenth century
X is the Roman numeral ten, a number

explanation.surface: A command to fasten an old monarch's figure to something.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex is to add or join something on, especially territory, so to attach.

clue.text: Axes rotten elm having woody tissue

explanation.surface: Axes chopping a decayed elm tree with its wood.

clue.text: He dictated ingredients of pepperoni

parts.note: joins, as in comes together with, gives MEETS
